clue.text: Clergyman provides remedy without a word of thanks for showing up

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: a remedy is a cure

indicators.note: in a down clue, showing up means the piece reads upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: TA is a British informal word for thank you

explanation.surface: A vicar hands out medicine but is annoyed when nobody turns up to say thank you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking; 'showing up' is the reversal signal in a down clue. TA is British slang for thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: A curate is an assistant parish priest, a junior member of the clergy.

clue.text: See great changes in economy travel

indicators.note: changes tells us the letters of the preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone notices big shifts in how cheap travel works.
explanation.definitionFit: Steerage was the cheapest class of passenger accommodation on a ship, the old equivalent of economy.

clue.text: Old soldier taking flight

parts.note: reads like a deserter running away, but means a bowman of old whose weapon sends feathered flights through the air

explanation.definitionFit: A bowman shoots arrows, whose feathered ends are called flights, and bowmen were soldiers in old armies.

clue.text: The notoriety only a hypochondriac would enjoy

definitions.text: The notoriety only a hypochondriac would enjoy

parts.words: The notoriety only a hypochondriac would enjoy
parts.note: a word for bad reputation read literally as being famous for being sick, which only someone who loves imagined illness would relish

explanation.definitionFit: Ill fame is an old phrase for a bad reputation, as in a house of ill fame.

clue.text: Father has wrinkles

parts.note: FR is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
to have something is to own it

explanation.surface: Dad is getting lines on his face.
explanation.definitionFit: Frowns are the furrows of the brow, so they are wrinkles in the face.

clue.text: No rise for those more advanced in service

indicators.note: for here means standing in for, so the letters of the two preceding words are exchanged into a new order

explanation.surface: Long-serving staff are told they will get no pay increase.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal is weak: 'for' implies the letters of NO RISE substitute in another order.
explanation.definitionFit: Senior describes someone higher in rank or longer in service than others.

clue.text: A stroke or a comma, maybe

definitions.meaning: a swimming stroke with both arms swung over together
the comma is a species of winged insect with a comma-shaped white mark

explanation.surface: Someone discusses whether a mark of punctuation counts as a stroke of the pen.
explanation.definitionFit: The swimming stroke and the insect family that includes the comma share this name.

clue.text: Such language is, to me, beyond comprehension

definitions.text: Such language is, to me, beyond comprehension

parts.words: Such language is, to me, beyond comprehension
parts.note: plays on the saying 'it's all ... to me', used of anything incomprehensible, naming the tongue of Athens

explanation.definitionFit: The language of Greece is proverbially the example of something impossible to understand.

clue.text: Improvised fashion garment

parts.note: to fashion is to make
a shift is a simple loose dress

explanation.surface: A designer throws together a dress on the spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Something makeshift is a temporary, improvised substitute.

clue.text: Mark II

parts.note: reads like a second model of a car, but pairs the first name of the American writer of Tom Sawyer with an old word for two

explanation.definitionFit: Mark is the pen name's first part and the old word for two completes it, so this surname fits both readings.

clue.text: Book in first-class accommodation for one in opposition

indicators.note: in places the book within the first-class letters

parts.note: A1 means first-class, with the 1 written as the letter I
NT is the New Testament, a book of the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone books a first-class cabin for a politician on the opposing side.
explanation.definitionFit: An anti is a person opposed to something, an opponent.

clue.text: Proceed to make good

definitions.meaning: to ... to a place is to go there
to fix or mend something broken

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to go ahead and put things right.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb has two unrelated senses: going somewhere and mending.

clue.text: Old cars go here for service

parts.note: the Mini is a classic small British car, so old cars are Minis
to have a go is to try

explanation.surface: Vintage vehicles are taken to a garage to be serviced.
explanation.definitionFit: A government department, such as one for defence, is a branch of public service; a ministry is also clergy service.

clue.text: How to secure a replay, for example?

definitions.meaning: to fasten something with a knot
a cup match, including one played again after a draw, is a cup fixture of this name

explanation.surface: Someone asks how a team might earn a second match.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to fasten, and in British football a knockout cup match is called this.

clue.text: Still up to date?

definitions.meaning: up to the present time, as in 'not so far'

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether something is still current.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means nevertheless and also so far, up to now.

clue.text: In short, a cheese parasite

parts.note: Brie is a soft French cheese
a fly can be a parasitic insect

explanation.surface: Put simply, an insect is feeding on the cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Briefly means in few words, in short.

clue.text: Advocates prohibition

definitions.meaning: barristers collectively are called the profession by this name

explanation.surface: Lawyers argue in favour of a ban.
explanation.definitionFit: Barristers as a body are known by this word, which also means a ban.

clue.text: Girl who could have a lead in opera

indicators.note: the girl's name, given the letter a at its front, would make the opera, so that leading letter goes; any backwards run of her name across these words is coincidence

parts.note: Aida is the Verdi opera

explanation.surface: A young woman might land the starring role in an opera.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'a lead' as the letter A placed in front: A plus the girl's name gives AIDA.
explanation.definitionFit: Ida is a feminine given name, so the definition is by example: a girl could be called this.

clue.text: Place where cubs may be left warm and dry

parts.note: to air laundry is to warm and dry it

explanation.surface: Young animals are left somewhere snug and dry.
explanation.definitionFit: A lair is a wild animal's den, where young such as lion or fox cubs live.

clue.text: Lyric writer bound to accept pound note

indicators.note: one piece accepts, i.e. takes in, the others

parts.note: girt means bound round, encircled
LB is the abbreviation for a pound in weight
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A songwriter is obliged to take a banknote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to accept' puts LBE inside GIRT. W.S. Gilbert wrote the words for Gilbert and Sullivan's comic operas.
explanation.definitionFit: W.S. Gilbert was the lyricist partner of composer Arthur Sullivan.

clue.text: Bird of ill omen to an old criminal?

definitions.meaning: a warbler with a dark crown

definitions.text: ill omen to an old criminal?
definitions.meaning: the black cloth an English judge put on before passing a death sentence

explanation.surface: Someone thinks a particular bird brings bad luck to an ageing crook.
explanation.definitionFit: It names a warbler and the cap a judge wore when sentencing a criminal to death.

clue.text: Fellow following Judah's son continuously

indicators.note: following places the fellow after Judah's son

parts.note: Onan was a son of Judah in Genesis
a don is a college fellow

explanation.surface: A man walks behind a biblical figure without stopping.
explanation.definitionFit: On and on is an idiom for without stopping, continuously.

clue.text: Response of soldiers being introduced to battle

indicators.note: the soldiers are introduced, i.e. put in front of, the battle

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, is a British army corps
action is fighting

explanation.surface: Troops respond to their first taste of combat.
explanation.definitionFit: A reaction is a response to something.

clue.text: Pardon and release

definitions.meaning: to let someone off a duty

explanation.surface: Someone is forgiven and freed.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to forgive and to exempt from an obligation.

clue.text: Horse and trap showing sign of neglect

parts.note: a cob is a sturdy short-legged horse
a spider's web is a trap

explanation.surface: An old horse-drawn carriage stands abandoned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trap' looks like the light carriage a horse pulls; here it is a snare.
explanation.definitionFit: Spider webs gather in places left uncleaned, so they show neglect.

clue.text: Father in pain, but brave

indicators.note: in places father inside the pain

parts.note: an ache is a pain
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: Dad is suffering but bearing it courageously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brave' looks like an adjective, but it is the noun for a Native American warrior.
explanation.definitionFit: A brave is a Native American warrior, and an Apache is one from that people.

clue.text: Horrified — has the wrong tag showing outside

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are on the outside of the other word
wrong signals the letters of tag are put out of order

explanation.surface: Someone is appalled to find a mislabelled item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' looks like a link word, but it is the piece the anagram of TAG (AGT, from 'wrong') surrounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Aghast means struck with horror, appalled.

clue.text: Housework to the French is fair game

parts.note: split as house and work: HO is an abbreviation for house and OP, short for opus, is a musical work
la is the feminine form of 'the' in French

explanation.surface: Doing the chores is considered fair game in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoopla is a fairground game of throwing rings over prizes.

clue.text: They don't go out with their mates

definitions.text: They don't go out with their mates

parts.words: They don't go out with their mates
parts.note: sounds like lonely people, but means workers who keep working when colleagues strike

explanation.definitionFit: Strikebreakers are given this insulting name by those on strike.

clue.text: Informed kin he won't be around

indicators.note: around signals the letters of the preceding words are moved about

explanation.surface: A family member is not going to be there.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in the know is an idiom for being informed.

clue.text: Sunbathed, topless, as requested

indicators.note: in an across clue topless means the first letter is removed

parts.note: to bask is to lie in the sun

explanation.surface: Someone sunbathes without a top, as they were asked to.
explanation.definitionFit: Asked is a synonym of requested.

clue.text: Law enforcer brings criminals before the board

indicators.note: before places the criminals ahead of the board

parts.note: cons are convicts
a table is a board

explanation.surface: A police officer takes offenders in front of a disciplinary committee.
explanation.definitionFit: A constable is a police officer.
